summary: Defines a MIME content type for sending files of MARC records, a standard format for library catalog information, in email and similar protocols. A MARC record holds metadata about a book or other resource. It is informational.

eli5.summary: It is a label that tells a mail program an attachment is a library's catalog cards, so it can be handed to the right software.

questions: how to send marc records by email
subtitle: MIME type registration for library catalog records in machine-readable format

tldr.problem: Libraries need a standard way to exchange catalog information (titles, authors, holdings, classifications) with other systems over networks and email, but no standard Internet media type existed for machine-readable catalog records.
tldr.mechanism: This memo defines and registers the application/marc MIME media type for files containing MARC records, a standardized format used by libraries for encoding bibliographic and related metadata. The format is based on ANSI Z39.2 and ISO 2709 standards.
tldr.outcome: The registered media type allows email, HTTP, and other protocols to properly label and handle library catalog data. Tools that receive such data now know to route it to library software rather than treating it as generic binary data.

today: RFC 2220 remains an Informational RFC. The application/marc media type is registered with IANA and used to label library catalog data in protocols such as HTTP and email.

sections.title: Introduction to MARC
sections.content: MARC stands for Machine-Readable Cataloging. MARC formats are sets of codes and content designators for encoding metadata for five types of library data: bibliographic (books and other resources), holdings (what a library owns), authority (names and subjects), classification (organization systems), and community information. The structure of MARC records implements national and international standards: ANSI Z39.2 (Information Interchange Format) and ISO 2709 (Format for Information Interchange). MARC is a communication format designed for the exchange of bibliographic information between different systems, though each system may store data in its own internal format.
sections.eli5: MARC is a way to write information about books and library stuff on a computer. Libraries share this information with each other using MARC records.

sections.title: The MARC Content Type
sections.content: This memo registers the MIME type application/marc for files containing MARC records in the harmonized USMARC and CANMARC specification. (The acronym USMARC stands for US MARC.) A complete MARC record must contain all three elements: the record structure, content designation, and data content according to the standard. No parameters are assigned to specific implementations or to particular types of MARC format, since the type is indicated in the Leader (a special field within each record). MARC records may contain long lines and arbitrary octet values, so base64 content-transfer-encoding is recommended for transmission over email.
sections.eli5: The media type is called application/marc. Files with this type hold complete library records. When sending them by email, the file should be encoded in a special way so it does not get corrupted.

sections.title: Security and Interoperability
sections.content: MARC data itself poses no known security risks to users. However, a MARC record may include or describe information marked with a security classification. This creates no risk to the reader of the MARC data, but it may present a security concern if classified information leaks from its source. MARC is designed as a communication format to enable interoperability between different systems that may use different internal storage formats. Each system remains free to store and display data locally as it prefers, while using MARC for exchange.
sections.eli5: MARC data is safe to read. But if someone sends secret information in a MARC record and the record leaks, the person who sent it could have a problem.
